_comment: PLACEHOLDER. This file is not a working prompt: the participant_ids mode
raises before it is ever read (see modes/participant_ids.py). It exists so the
mode's prompt_config_path points somewhere real, and so whoever finishes the
mode has the shape in front of them.
The loader (prompt.py load_prompt_config) wants 'system_prompt' plus
'user_prompt_template'. If the template is absent it assembles one from
'intro' / 'questions' / 'examples' instead -- see the participant_image config
beside this file for a worked example of both halves.
Templates are rendered against the record's flattened fields, so {participant}
and {conversation_floor} already resolve to the ids without any code change;
{record_json} is the whole record, and an unknown placeholder is left as-is.
TODO: write a template that names people by id and says what carries those ids
visually. Two things to settle while writing it:
- Whether the floor speakers are named individually. They arrive as ONE mixed
soundtrack, so naming them implies the mix is no longer anonymous and the
prompt has to say what the listener can and cannot separate.
- Where the media placeholders actually land. The participant_image prompt
writes '<image>' / '<audio1>' / '<audio2>' as literal text while the real
tokens are emitted at the parts' positions, ahead of the text block, so
those markers resolve to nothing. Either interleave text between the parts
in build_turn(), or describe them strictly by order.
system_prompt: You are a helpful multimodal assistant.
user_prompt_template: TODO: unwritten. The participant_ids mode is a placeholder; see modes/participant_ids.py.
